interface.title: NeRV – Neuroimaging Results Visualization
interface.field: Neuroimaging / reproducibility of image-processing pipelines (continuous testing on CBRAIN)
interface.stage_of_work: Quality control and comparison of processed results across pipelines, after processing has run
interface.what_it_is_for: Browse continuous-testing results for each neuroimaging experiment, compare how two pipelines (e.g. FSL vs FreeSurfer) measured one metric, such as hippocampus volume, and open the per-subject pipeline provenance, including pass/fail status and CBRAIN IDs, behind any odd result.

data.note: The server ships with two experiment directories, each holding one dataset file: compass-nd (pipelines CSM and IZK, 2864 datapoints, 0 missing; values look uniformly random and synthetic) and prevent-AD (pipelines FSL and FreeSurfer, 2864 datapoints, 158 missing: FSL 90, FreeSurfer 68). The prevent-AD data look realistic. The only metric shown is Hippocampus Volume (mm³). Nothing was uploaded. The app has no upload control.

tree.general: Check whether different processing pipelines give consistent measurements for each dataset, and trace suspicious results back to their processing records
tree.specific: Use NeRV to compare hippocampus-volume results across pipelines for compass-nd and prevent-AD, and open the CBRAIN provenance of outliers and failures

features.name: Pairwise method-comparison joint plot with linked record view

features.specific: The Joint Plot tab has x and y Dataset-Pipeline dropdowns offering the same options (picking one pipeline for both axes gives y=x), a scatter with marginal histograms and an x range slider. Clicking a point fills a Metadata card with each pipeline's subject, result and steps; the records are looked up by result value, not by subject, so tied values (e.g. failed = −1) can show different subjects for the two pipelines
